account: It is day 0, just after one, and I have returned to town hall for the scheduled town accounts. I spent the morning at the market and went home for the noon lunch appointment. I am now beside the treasury chest, but have not yet inspected its contents. Nothing I have learned establishes a secret gathering or unusual scheme. Several townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery. Townsfolk 08 and 28 also reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread at the inn. I saw the baker carrying bread at the market and putting bread into the bakery stall chest. These movements could simply be baking, stocking the stall, and supplying the inn; I do not know of another purpose. The repeated reports are not necessarily independent evidence of anything suspicious. A lantern also appeared inside town hall this morning; I do not know who placed it or why. The unresolved matter is my three o'clock tea appointment: the appointment book names a neighbour at a dockside cottage on the east bank, but gives neither a name nor an exact cottage. The secretary said she would inquire. She had no correspondence or town news to report earlier. I still feel I might be missing something, but that is a feeling rather than evidence. My next priorities are the accounts and getting the secretary's clarification so I can keep the tea appointment.
